payload.text: I read this as a stack-economics research task: compare cost-optimal stack options for the greenfield student startup, with evidence, ruthless anti-overengineering, ending with ## EXPAND. Plan: survey repo context for what the product actually is, gather pricing/evidence via search, then synthesize the comparison.

Product context confirmed: it's a Korean AI presentation-agent PWA (PPTX/PDF + streaming STT + event-driven RAG/LLM, presenter console / audience screen split). Let me extract the application PDF for budget/scale constraints and pull current pricing evidence in parallel.
PDF uses CID fonts — need a proper extractor. Let me check for pdftotext/PyMuPDF, and retry web search.

Budget confirmed: **500,000 KRW (~US$365) total** for 2026.6~2027.3, 4-5 fourth-year students, a university SW competition project. Let me read the rest of the application for scale/storage requirements.

Full picture acquired. Key constraints: **500,000 KRW (~$365) total budget**, 9-month window, 5 students, scale target ~10 concurrent demo users, budget line mostly earmarked for ChatGPT/API costs. Now let me gather pricing evidence for each stack component.
web_search is down. Falling back to direct pricing-page fetches — these are the authoritative sources anyway.
Two key data points secured (Supabase Free, Cloudflare Workers Free incl. R2/D1/KV/Vectorize). Now fetching Vercel, Deepgram, OpenAI, Upstash pricing in parallel.
Vercel Hobby (1M edge req/mo, 100GB transfer, 1M invocations, 4h CPU, 1GB Blob — free) and Deepgram ($200 credit, Nova-3 streaming promo $0.0048/min) secured. Now OpenAI API and Upstash.

OpenAI pricing secured (gpt-5-mini $0.25/$2.00, gpt-5-nano $0.05/$0.40, Whisper $0.006/min, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe $0.003/min, embedding-3-small $0.02/M). Upstash free tier (256MB, 500K cmd/mo). Last evidence pair: PostHog and Sentry free tiers.
All core pricing evidence is in. One last verification: Deepgram Korean language support (critical for this product).

All evidence gathered. Nova-3 confirmed for Korean (`ko`, `ko-KR`) streaming — and notably **Flux does NOT support Korean** (10 languages only), a critical vendor-selection fact. Now synthesizing the full report and sending to the lead.
Report delivered to the lead. Cleaning up my temp extraction files, then ending the turn.

Stack-economics report complete and delivered to the lead.

**Key findings:**
- **$0/month infra is correct for this project** — Supabase Free (Postgres + pgvector + Realtime + Storage + Auth + Edge Functions, no CPU-time cap) covers every backend need at 10 concurrent users; verified against supabase.com/pricing.
- **STT: Deepgram Nova-3 with `language=ko`** — officially supports Korean streaming; $200 free credit ≈ 41K minutes (project needs ~600); promo streaming $0.0048/min. Flagged that the newer Flux model does **not** support Korean.
- **LLM: gpt-5-mini / gpt-5-nano + gpt-4o-mini for VLM** — total project AI spend ≈ $5-20, i.e. the application's ~477,000 KRW ChatGPT-subscription budget line is 10-40x overkill.
- **Rejected with evidence:** Cloudflare Workers free for the orchestrator (10ms CPU cap), Vectorize (docs say paid-only — contradiction flagged), WebRTC, Redis, queues, VPS self-hosting, dedicated vector DB, multi-vendor observability.
- **11 leads raised** including the 5s-SLA latency budget, Supabase 1-week pause demo risk, python-pptx runtime question, Vercel 1-seat limitation, and Deepgram Korean accuracy benchmark.

Evidence sources: supabase.com/pricing, developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing, vercel.com/pricing, deepgram.com/pricing, platform.openai.com/docs/pricing, upstash.com/pricing, posthog.com/pricing, sentry.io/pricing, plus the application PDF (500K KRW budget, ~10 concurrent users). Ended with ## EXPAND covering Korean-STT A/B benchmarks, OpenAI KR-card onboarding, post-demo production cost sensitivity, and Supabase storage size limits.

I read this as a verification pass: (1) harden every price/limit claim with direct URLs + access date + measured-vs-assumed separation, (2) resolve the Python parsing question with evidence. Fetching the three missing sources now: Supabase Edge Functions docs (runtime/limits), Cloud Run free tier, Render free tier.

Both facts verified: Supabase Edge Functions are **TypeScript/Deno only** (official docs) — Python parsing cannot run there. Cloud Run free tier measured: 2M req/mo, 180K vCPU-sec, 360K GiB-sec, with a **Seoul region** (asia-northeast3). Sending the refined, evidence-hardened report.

Verification pass complete, sent to the lead.

**What changed:**
- **Full claims registry** — every figure tagged MEASURED (fetched verbatim 2026-08-13, direct URL per claim) vs ASSUMED (volumes, FX, latency, budget-line reading) vs UNKNOWN (Sentry free error quota). No figure was wrong, but now the temporal risk is explicit and the measured set is the diff base for re-checks at milestones.
- **Python parser resolved with evidence:** Supabase Edge Functions are officially TypeScript/Deno-only, so python-pptx cannot run there. Recommendation: local parse script on upload for MVP (parsing is an admin action, not in the 5s live path); Cloud Run free tier (measured 2M req/180K vCPU-sec/mo, Seoul region exists) if server-side parsing becomes necessary — a deck parse uses ~0.7% of the free tier. Also flagged the VLM implication: python-pptx can't render slides, so the worker needs LibreOffice headless, and slide VLM analysis should run once at upload time (cheapest ordering, keeps live path LLM-only).
- **Updated ## CLAIMS** (8 compact claims, each statused) and **## EXPAND** (8 items, leading with the Deepgram-vs-Vito-vs-Clova Korean benchmark and token-volume measurement).
